message.content:
**Texas Traffic Laws – Key Points (as of 2024)** | Topic | Summary | |-------|---------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits range from 35 mph on rural roads to 75 mph on interstates.
• Speed limit enforcement uses radar, lidar, and automated cameras. | | **Seat Belt & Child Restraint** | • All occupants must wear seat belts; failure can result in a $50 fine.
• Children under 8 must use a child safety seat; those 8–15 must use a booster. | | **DUI / DWI** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal for drivers over 21.
• Lower BAC limits apply to commercial drivers (0.04%) and drivers under 21 (0.02%).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, mandatory education, and possible jail time. | | **Texting & Phone Use** | • Texting while driving is prohibited for all drivers.
• Hands‑free phone use is allowed but still subject to safe‑driving standards. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, vehicles approaching from the right have priority.
• Pedestrians always have priority at crosswalks. | | **Lane Discipline** | • Drivers must stay within their lane unless turning or passing.
• Passing on the right is generally prohibited except when the vehicle ahead is turning left. | | **School Bus** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus stops to pick up or drop off children. | | **Traffic Signals & Signs** | • Red lights mean stop; green means proceed (unless otherwise directed).
• Yellow lights indicate caution; drivers should prepare to stop if safe. | | **Parking Regulations** | • Parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or on sidewalks is prohibited.
• Parking in designated handicapped spaces requires a valid permit. | | **Vehicle Equipment** | • Headlights must be used between sunset and sunrise, during inclement weather, and when visibility is reduced.
• Mirrors must be properly adjusted. | ### How to Find Specific Statutes - **Texas Transportation Code**: The primary source for traffic laws. - **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)**: Offers guides, FAQs, and updates on law changes. - **County Sheriff’s Office**: Local ordinances may add additional restrictions (e.g., speed limits, parking rules). ### Important Notes - **Legal Advice**: This overview is informational only and does not constitute legal advice. For specific legal questions, consult a licensed attorney. - **Updates**: Traffic laws can change; always verify current statutes before relying on them. If you need details on a particular aspect—such as DUI penalties, seat belt enforcement, or local ordinances—let me know!
